title: Garlic-Scallion Chicken Skewers
shortDescription: Chicken-thigh pieces are marinated with soy, garlic, scallion, and sesame, threaded evenly, and grilled until every piece reaches 165°F / 74°C.
culturalContext: Dak-kkochi refers broadly to Korean chicken skewers, which vary in cut, sauce, street-food presentation, and heat. This garlic-scallion version is a contemporary grilled adaptation.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

ingredients.preparation: cut into even 3 cm / 1.25-inch pieces; do not wash

mixOrder: Combine soy sauce and rice syrup.
Add garlic, scallions, sesame oil, and pepper.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 8 hours without test-cook approval.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before the marinade contacts raw chicken.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw chicken; do not use it on cooked food.
substitutions: If wooden skewers are used, follow manufacturer soaking and heat limits; metal is preferred for this draft.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.

instructions.heading: Cut without washing
instructions.action: Cut chicken into even pieces on a dedicated board; do not wash raw chicken.
instructions.safetyNote: Washing raw poultry can spread contamination.

instructions.heading: Mix marinade
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any serving sauce before raw contact.

instructions.heading: Marinate cold
instructions.action: Coat chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate poultry at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Thread and preheat
instructions.action: With clean flat metal skewers, thread pieces loosely with small gaps; preheat medium and cooler grill zones.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are evenly spaced and skewer handles remain accessible.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash hands after threading and sanitize the work area.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify throughout
instructions.action: Grill, turning all sides, until representative pieces at both ends and center of every skewer reach 165°F / 74°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean tongs and check more than one piece per skewer.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve carefully
instructions.action: Transfer skewers to a clean platter, rest 3 minutes, and warn diners that metal skewers are hot and sharp.
instructions.safetyNote: Prevent burns and puncture injuries; remove chicken from skewers for children.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with medium direct and cooler zones; place handles away from flame and separate raw and cooked tools.
targetInternalTemperature: 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part of every chicken piece.
visualDonenessCues: Surface is browned without burned sugar
foodSafetyNotes: Keep chicken at or below 40°F / 4°C and prevent cross-contact.
Cook every piece to 165°F / 74°C with a clean calibrated thermometer.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels.

substitutions: If wooden skewers are used, follow manufacturer soaking and heat limits; metal is preferred for this draft.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
ingredientSourcing: Choose cold chicken thighs in intact packaging and transport them home promptly.
makeAhead: Mix marinade up to 2 days ahead; marinate chicken only within the stated refrigerated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked chicken in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending review.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and fresh vegetables; remove from skewers for safer child service.

faq.question: Why check multiple pieces on each skewer?
faq.answer: End and center pieces may cook at different rates.

faq.question: Can I use wooden skewers?
faq.answer: Metal is preferred; wooden skewers require manufacturer-directed soaking and burn control.
